Zhitao Liu刘志涛

Postdoctoral Researcher · Human Geography

Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences

I study how urban and rural settlements evolve, and what these changes mean for ecosystems and environmental sustainability. My research connects settlement mapping with the ecological consequences of land-use change, from regional patterns to global comparisons.

Research focus

Settlements, ecosystems & a changing planet

01

Urban & rural settlements

Mapping settlement patterns and comparing the spatial and temporal dynamics of urban and rural expansion.

02

Land change & ecological impacts

Understanding how settlement expansion affects biodiversity, ecosystem services and the ecological environment.

03

Resilience & sustainability

Exploring urban resilience, environmental governance and integrated frameworks for tracking sustainability.

About me

I am a postdoctoral researcher in human geography at the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences, working with Prof. Chuanglin Fang. I received my Ph.D. in Human Geography from the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences in 2025, and my bachelor's degree in Human Geography and Urban–Rural Planning from Sun Yat-sen University in 2020.
